name: archive_probe
description: Say what an archive or a document shows about its own protection, and what it does not. ZIP: structural, read by this tool from the bytes: the End Of Central Directory record, the Zip64 end record wherever a Zip64 locator sits before it (whatever the End record says, as zipfile follows it), and each central directory entry (empty and self-extracting archives included): per-member encryption, the WinZip AES extra field, DOS times with their raw words and no zone; a name that is not valid UTF-8 is shown escaped and does not hide the other members. 7-Zip: listed through the installed 7z (bounded, no password prompt, ended with the tool) where there is one, giving the members, each one's encrypted flag and whether the header is encrypted; the start header is read and its checksums checked, and a byte search is kept as a hint only when 7z is absent or cannot read the file. RAR: identified, protection not determined. PDF and OLE/Office: a heuristic byte search for markers, reported with offsets, never as 'not encrypted' and never as a verdict (the structural document reader is not provided by this pack). Whether member names are readable is a finding separate from whether the data is encrypted. Nothing is extracted. What is loaded is bounded by max_metadata_bytes whatever the file's own headers declare: a ZIP whose central directory is declared larger than the bound (in the End record or the Zip64 record), larger than the file, or with more entries than the bound holds at 46 bytes each is not listed and says so; the directory is read in blocks, so memory does not follow its size. A PDF or an OLE file is searched whole, in a linear pass (bytes_searched and search_complete say so), because a PDF's marker sits at its end. The tool has its own clock (max_seconds, default 100, below the timeout of 120): at it, or on SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP, it ends the 7z it started and answers once (status partial or interrupted, exit 128 + the signal). Every answer carries status and status_basis. SENSITIVE: member names, 7-Zip header strings, the 7z diagnostics and the path are evidence text. A part of one shaped like an identifier or a secret (a run of 10 digits or more, letters and digits of 8 or more, grouped digits, a recovery password, password=... , user-info, vendor tokens) is replaced by a marker in the answer and in every file it names (names_withheld counts them), the rest of the name stays; a second check of the output replaces what the first let through and makes the answer partial. Withholding is by shape, measured on 2,000 random draws per shape planted in a member name or path (rates, not guarantees): hexadecimal ids of 16, 32 and 64, numbers of 10 digits or more, recovery passwords written with dashes, spaces, dots, underscores or no separator, AWS access key ids, password= and api_key: assignments, user-info, and 4x4 groups of capitals and digits joined by - or . : printed whole in 0 draws; random mixed-case letters and digits of 8, 12 or 40 characters 0 draws, of 9 about 1.4%, of 16 about 0.6%; random lowercase letters and digits of 8 about 7%, of 12 about 2.4%, of 16 about 0.4%; 24 random letters about 2%, a 16-character base32 id about 3.4%, four groups of four lowercase hexadecimal digits joined by underscores about 8%, a full-width id 0 draws. NOT recognised, by design: an identifier of 7 characters or fewer, a number of 9 digits or fewer, a lowercase-only run of up to 22 letters (it reads as a word), a secret of any other shape; a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. It also changes names that are not secrets: of the file names of a documents tree 6.9% have a part withheld (10-digit timestamps, UUIDs) and 0.6% of its directories, of an application tree 16% and 3.1% (a word with a digit inside, such as libmp3lame, is withheld in part).

path.description: A ZIP, 7-Zip, RAR, PDF or OLE document

limit.description: Members (or 7-Zip header strings) shown inline (default 200); all of them are counted, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

max_metadata_bytes.description: The most container metadata to load or search: a ZIP central directory, a 7-Zip header (default 33554432, at least 4096). A ZIP whose central directory is declared larger (in either end record), larger than the file, or with more entries than this holds at 46 bytes each is not listed and says so. It does not bound the search of a PDF or an OLE file, which is always whole

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 100, 1 to 110; the manifest's timeout is 120). At it the 7z is ended and the answer says what was not read
